about: Varied, non-repetitive ~3 minute talking-head script for the local long e2e (scripts/e2e-video-motion.py --long). Kokoro TTS (af_heart) speaks each 'speech' part; 'gap' parts are digital-silence pauses in seconds. Five deliberate 'Um,' fillers and several 1 s pauses.
parts: Good morning. Today I want to walk you through how we plan a small vegetable garden on a city balcony.
The first thing to check is sunlight, because most fruiting plants need at least six hours of direct sun every day.
if your balcony faces north, focus on leafy greens like spinach, lettuce and chard instead of tomatoes.
Next, think about weight. Wet soil is heavy, so ask your building manager how much load the balcony can safely carry.
Fabric grow bags are lighter than ceramic pots, and they let roots breathe during hot summer afternoons.
Water is the third question. A small drip line on a cheap battery timer saves you from watering by hand twice a day.
I learned that the hard way during a heatwave, when half of my basil wilted in a single weekend.
Now let's talk about soil. Buy a peat-free potting mix and blend in some compost for slow, steady nutrition.
Never use garden dirt in containers. It compacts quickly, drains badly, and often carries pests and weed seeds.
For seeds, start with quick wins: radishes are ready in about four weeks, and peas climb happily up a simple string trellis.
herbs are another easy success. Mint spreads aggressively, so give it a pot of its own.
Pollination matters too. On a high floor there may be few bees, so gently shake tomato flowers or brush them with a soft paintbrush.
Keep a simple notebook. Write down what you planted, when it sprouted, and how much you harvested each week.
After one season, those notes become your own local guide, far more useful than any generic calendar online.
one more tip about wind: tall plants on an exposed corner need sturdy stakes and soft ties, or they snap in the first storm.
Let me summarize the plan. Check the sun, respect the weight limit, automate the watering, and choose good container soil.
Then start with fast crops, help pollination by hand, and record everything you observe.
that is really all you need to begin. Thanks for watching, and send me a photo of your first harvest.
